claims.source_doc: Whitepaper §3 / Benchmark table / Pitch deck slide 5
claims.claim: Frame time 8-16 ms (60-120 FPS at 8K) on classical GPU substrate.
claims.current_best: CPU reference path measured 2.68 s at 8K (v3.1, 1.77x over v3.0); the documented 8-16 ms number requires a bound GPU device, which no committed run has had (fail-closed lane reports measured:false).

claims.current_best: 4 spp traced at 8K: 11.16 s, hits 1,833,696, antialiases 1,584 silhouette pixels; exact per-sample oracle reproduction in tests.

claims.claim: Scenes with multiple objects, materials and lights render as composed scenes.
claims.current_best: v3.2 composite elevation: nearest-hit composition across sphere/box/plane objects; two-sphere and studio scenes measured at 1080p and 8K; single-sphere baseline path bit-identical.

claims.source_doc: Benchmark table ('GI quality: perfect by construction')
claims.current_best: Honest relabelling stands: the validated demo scene resolves 32 distinct distribution values; 'perfect' is the mathematical design goal of the exact-diagonalisation pipeline, not a measured frame property. The code path (exact dense eigendecomposition, no Monte Carlo, no denoiser) is the construction the documents describe.
claims.gate_to_measured: Define and measure an accepted GI-error metric (e.g. vs an analytic reference scene) so 'perfect' becomes a number.

claims.source_doc: Whitepaper §3 / Benchmark table ('Memory compression 11.5x via PULVINI')
claims.claim: 11.5x memory compression on the final frame buffer.
claims.current_best: The v33 render path measures raster_compression_ratio (3,628,800x on the demo scene: parametric state vs dense frame) -- an ordinary procedural-vs-raster ratio, NOT the 11.5x PULVINI phi-fold claim. PULVINI folding is a separate (enterprise/mining) plane capability and is not asserted by this artifact.
claims.gate_to_measured: Run the PULVINI fold over a rendered frame on its owning plane and commit that plane's measured artifact.
